news.og_desc: George Washington was the U.S. president who initially established Thanksgiving as a national holiday. He did so on October 3, 1789, when he declared that the national government would be celebrating Thanksgiving Day on the 26th day of the following month. John Adams and James Madison echoed Washington's declaration. It didn't entirely stick at that point in the nation's history — but decades later, when President Lincoln made a similar declaration, Americans heeded his call to action.
